item.title: DNA nanomachine strategy reverses chemoresistance in small cell lung cancer
item.description: Professor Chao Zhang's team at Zhujiang Hospital, Southern Medical University, has developed a novel DNA nanomachine-based drug delivery and release strategy aimed at overcoming chemoresistance in small cell lung cancer (SCLC).

item.title: New European project develops human-based models for brain disorders
item.description: The University of Barcelona is consolidating its position at the forefront of European research thanks to the strategic project "VISI-ON-BRAIN: Cutting-edge Human In Vitro and In Silico Biomedical Tools on Brain Disorders".

item.title: Research reveals nuclear metabolic fingerprint in human cells
item.description: More than two hundred metabolic enzymes, many of which are normally tasked with producing energy in the mitochondria, are also found sitting directly on top of human DNA, according to a study published today in Nature Communications.

item.title: Disrupted iron levels after SARS-CoV-2 infection may trigger long COVID
item.description: Problems with iron levels in the blood and the body's ability to regulate this important nutrient as a result of SARS-CoV-2 infection could be a key trigger for long COVID, new research has discovered.

item.title: PET imaging reveals molecular mechanism behind ketamine's antidepressant effects
item.description: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide, and approximately 30% of patients develop treatment-resistant depression (TRD), a condition that does not respond adequately to conventional antidepressant therapies.

item.title: Virtual immunostaining method improves detection of vascular invasion in thyroid cancer
item.description: In a groundbreaking study published in BME Frontiers, researchers from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), in collaboration with international partners, have developed a deep learning-based virtual multiplexed immunostaining (mIHC) method.

item.title: Brain cells amplify important signals to guide focus and navigation
item.description: Nerve cells in the brain are constantly bombarded with information from different senses simultaneously. How can the brain prioritize what is most important?

item.title: Meaning, purpose and spirituality should be core parts of healthcare, say experts
item.description: A new peer-reviewed paper calls for meaning, purpose, and spirituality to be treated as core components of lifestyle medicine - not optional add-ons - because they directly influence patients' ability to adopt and sustain health-promoting behaviors.

item.title: NIH grant supports research on immune-related receptor in neurons
item.description: Florida Atlantic University has received a $2.4 million grant from the National Institutes of Health to investigate how an immune-related receptor in neurons plays a fundamental role in brain function, behavior and psychiatric health.

item.title: Wnt signaling in fibroblasts drives gastric cancer metastasis to the liver
item.description: Researchers at the Cancer Research Institute and the Nano Life Science Institute (WPI-NanoLSI), Kanazawa University, have uncovered a critical mechanism that enables gastric cancer to spread to distant organs.
